summary: Grux 0.2.0 leaks the AWS secret access key in full and is quadratic on attacker-chosen input
description:
**Description**

0.2.0 fixed the two 0.1.0 criticals and introduced two defects of its own.

**1. Base64 blindness leaks the AWS secret access key.** `/` was dropped from the entropy
alphabet to stop file paths being destroyed. Standard base64 is `A-Za-z0-9+/`, so removing
`/` also removed it from base64, and an AWS secret access key containing `/` went out in
full. This is the canonical example, not the only one: any base64 credential carrying a `/`
is affected.

**2. A quadratic scan on hostile input.** The PEM pattern's lazy scan meant every `BEGIN`
marker rescanned the rest of the document. **1.2MB of hostile input took 72 seconds.**

0.2.0 also carries the defects listed under Advisory 3, which apply to the whole 0.2.x line.

**Impact**

An AWS secret access key present in text handed to `SecretRedactor` reaches the model
provider verbatim. That is a full credential for the account it belongs to.

Separately, any caller that redacts attacker-influenced text, which is the intended use, can
be stalled by a document full of `BEGIN` markers. Scored on its own that is
`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`, 7.5 High.

**Patches**

The denial of service was fixed in 0.2.1. The credential leak was fixed in 0.3.0, which
introduced a path heuristic that discards 14% of AWS secret access keys, see Advisory 4.
Move to **0.5.0**.

**Workarounds**

None.

**References**

`CHANGELOG.md` sections 0.2.0, 0.2.1 and 0.3.0.
